main.title: Ben-Hur
main.subtitle: A broken friendship becomes a struggle against Roman power
main.summary: William Wyler's Ben-Hur turns Lew Wallace's novel into a widescreen epic of betrayal, endurance and revenge. Charlton Heston plays Judah Ben-Hur, a Jewish nobleman whose friendship with the Roman officer Messala collapses under the demands of imperial rule. The film premiered in New York on 18 November 1959 after a production based at Rome's Cinecittà studios.

cards.heading: An epic built around a friendship
cards.text: William Wyler's Ben-Hur turns Lew Wallace's novel into a widescreen epic of betrayal, endurance and revenge. Charlton Heston plays Judah Ben-Hur, a Jewish nobleman whose friendship with the Roman officer Messala collapses under the demands of imperial rule. The film premiered in New York on 18 November 1959 after a production based at Rome's Cinecittà studios.

cards.heading: Judah and Messala
cards.text: Messala wants Judah's help in controlling the local population. Their disagreement leaves a personal wound that Roman authority makes far more dangerous. Judah's punishment separates him from his family and carries the story through slavery at sea, survival and a return to confront his former friend. The changing scale matters: private loyalties repeatedly meet the machinery of an empire. Scenes of crowds and military power make the consequences of the two men's conflict visible around them.

cards.heading: Making the contest visible
cards.text: The chariot race gives that conflict a physical arena. Horses, wheels and the distance between competitors provide clear points of attention as the race grows more dangerous. Its action depends on the viewer understanding where Judah and Messala are in relation to one another. MGM Camera 65 photography gives the spectacle a wide frame, while Miklós Rózsa's score supplies the larger drama with recurring themes. The film joins that immense production scale to a story about what revenge costs its survivor.

main.title: Laser
main.summary: Theodore Maiman built the first laser at Hughes Research Laboratories in 1960, following theoretical work on optical amplification.

cards.heading: Laser
cards.text: Theodore Maiman built the first laser at Hughes Research Laboratories in 1960, following theoretical work on optical amplification. A laser amplifies light through stimulated emission, producing a coherent beam. That coherence allows light to remain narrow over distance or be focused into a very small spot. These properties support uses ranging from communication and pointers to cutting and lithography. The device's name abbreviates light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation, describing the process that gives it such precise control over light.

main.title: The first PDP-1 is delivered
main.summary: Digital Equipment Corporation delivered its first PDP-1 in 1960, following its development in 1959. The computer became important to early hacker culture and later ran Steve Russell's Spacewar!.

cards.heading: The first PDP-1 is delivered
cards.text:
Digital Equipment Corporation delivered its first PDP-1 in 1960, following its development in 1959. The computer became important to early hacker culture and later ran Steve Russell's Spacewar!.

The PDP-1 (Programmed Data Processor-1) is the first computer in Digital Equipment Corporation's PDP series and was first produced in 1959. It is known for being the most important computer in the creation of hacker culture at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Bolt, Beranek and Newman, and elsewhere. The PDP-1 is the original hardware for one of the first video games, Steve Russell's 1962 game Spacewar!.

main.title: Psycho
main.summary: Alfred Hitchcock's Psycho reached cinemas in 1960, following embezzler Marion Crane to the motel run by Norman Bates.

cards.heading: Psycho
cards.text: Alfred Hitchcock's Psycho reached cinemas in 1960, following embezzler Marion Crane to the motel run by Norman Bates. Her disappearance draws her sister, her lover and a private investigator into the story. Joseph Stefano adapted Robert Bloch's novel, with Janet Leigh and Anthony Perkins in the central roles. Hitchcock used a modest budget, black-and-white photography and the crew from his television series. Critics initially divided over its subject, but enormous audience interest made it a commercial success and encouraged a major reassessment of the film.

main.title: Berlin Wall
main.summary: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall on 13 August 1961 to stop its citizens fleeing west.

cards.heading: Berlin Wall
cards.text: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall on 13 August 1961 to stop its citizens fleeing west. The barrier encircled West Berlin, separating it from East Berlin and the surrounding German Democratic Republic. Concrete walls, watchtowers and a heavily defended strip turned the division into a physical obstacle to movement. East German authorities presented it as protection against hostile forces; West Berlin's mayor Willy Brandt called it a Wall of Shame. It remained a guarded boundary until 1989, defining everyday life in the divided city.

main.title: Catch-22
main.summary: Joseph Heller published his first novel, Catch-22, in 1961 after beginning it in 1953.

cards.heading: Catch-22
cards.text: Joseph Heller published his first novel, Catch-22, in 1961 after beginning it in 1953. Set during World War II, it follows American bombardier Captain John Yossarian and a fictional squadron based on Pianosa in the Mediterranean. Events appear out of sequence and return through different characters' perspectives, gradually building the timeline. This fractured structure carries a satire of military bureaucracy and greed. The war provides both the setting and the system surrounding Yossarian, while the shifting narration lets its contradictions accumulate across the novel.

main.title: Vostok 1
main.summary: On 12 April 1961, Vostok 1 carried Yuri Gagarin into the first human orbit of Earth.

cards.heading: Vostok 1
cards.text:
Vostok 1 (Russian: Восток, lit. 'East' or 'Orient') was the first spaceflight of the Vostok programme and the first human orbital spaceflight in history. The Vostok 3KA space capsule was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome on 12 April 1961, with Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin aboard, making him the first human to reach orbital velocity around the Earth and to complete a full orbit around the Earth.

The orbital spaceflight consisted of a single orbit around the Earth that reached a maximum altitude of 327 kilometers (203 miles; 177 nautical miles) and a minimum of 181 kilometers (112 miles; 98 nautical miles). The flight took 108 minutes from launch to landing. Gagarin parachuted to the ground separately from his capsule after ejecting at 7 km (23,000 ft) altitude.

main.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
main.summary: The United States and Soviet Union confronted each other over nuclear missiles in Cuba from 16 to 28 October 1962.

cards.heading: Cuban Missile Crisis
cards.text: The United States and Soviet Union confronted each other over nuclear missiles in Cuba from 16 to 28 October 1962. Soviet deployments there followed American missile placements within range of Moscow in Britain, Italy and Turkey. Relations with Cuba had already deteriorated after the failed American-backed invasion of 1961 and subsequent sabotage. For thirteen days, the dispute brought the Cold War close to nuclear war. The crisis exposed how weapons positioned around rival states could turn regional confrontation into a threat with worldwide consequences.

main.title: Lawrence of Arabia
main.subtitle: A desert campaign becomes a study of ambition and divided loyalties
main.summary: David Lean's Lawrence of Arabia follows British officer T.E. Lawrence during the First World War and the Arab revolt against Ottoman rule. Peter O'Toole plays a man drawn toward both the desert and an extraordinary image of himself. Released in 1962, the film combines a military epic with a study of a participant whose motives and loyalties remain unsettled.

cards.heading: An officer and his legend
cards.text: David Lean's Lawrence of Arabia follows British officer T.E. Lawrence during the First World War and the Arab revolt against Ottoman rule. Peter O'Toole plays a man drawn toward both the desert and an extraordinary image of himself. Released in 1962, the film combines a military epic with a study of a participant whose motives and loyalties remain unsettled.

cards.heading: The power of a reputation
cards.text: Lawrence's campaign depends on negotiations as much as daring journeys. Meetings with Arab leaders and British officials expose different expectations of what victory will bring. His growing reputation can unite people around an operation, but it also feeds his belief in his own exceptional role. The film lets that confidence become increasingly troubling. O'Toole's performance keeps personal exhilaration, uncertainty and cruelty close together, giving the campaign a human centre that does not remain comfortably heroic.

cards.heading: Distance, spectacle and politics
cards.text: Freddie Young's wide desert photography makes distance part of the drama. A figure approaching across an immense landscape changes the scale of an encounter before the characters speak. Lean carries that command of space into battles and crowded political meetings, while Maurice Jarre's music gives the journey a sweeping identity. The contrast between vast landscapes and tense negotiations is essential: the adventure that creates Lawrence's public legend is inseparable from the competing powers directing the war.

main.title: Amazing Fantasy #15
main.summary: Amazing Fantasy #15 introduced Spider-Man in its August 1962 issue.

cards.heading: Amazing Fantasy #15
cards.text: Amazing Adult Fantasy, retitled Amazing Fantasy in its final issue, is an American comic book anthology series published by Marvel Comics from 1961 through 1962, with the latter title revived with superhero features in 1995 and in the 2000s. The final 1960s issue, Amazing Fantasy #15 (cover-dated Aug. 1962), introduced the popular superhero Spider-Man who would go on to become one of the most famous superheroes of all time. Amazing Adult Fantasy premiered with issue #7, taking over the numbering from Amazing Adventures.
